authors: Al Marshad H, Moiseff A, Corless A
title: Structure and Function of the Compound Eye in Photinus Carolinus (Lampyridae): Regional Variation and Visual Performance
why: Open-access proceedings paper on two male and two female Photinus carolinus; its Table 2 gives an interommatidial angle (about 0.04 rad in females, 0.05 rad in males), a sampling frequency and a cut-off frequency by eye region, but the fetch tool returned the table garbled and no sentence states the value, so no verbatim quote could be taken. A person reading the PDF can log interommatidial_deg and a sampling-based acuity for Photinus carolinus.

authors: Harry J. Grossman, Robert B. Northrop
title: Tests of the limiting visual resolution of the DCMD system of the lubber grasshopper to rectangular gratings
why: The title says it tests the limiting resolution to gratings in the lubber grasshopper, which is Romalea microptera; the page did not open and the abstract was empty in OpenAlex, so authors, volume and pages are not confirmed and it is not known that the paper names the species. If it gives a limiting grating frequency it closes acuity_cpd for Romalea. Authors from the Crossref record (desk Crossref run 3, 18 October 2026).

authors: Tyrrell LP, Goller B, Moore BA, Altshuler DL, Fernandez-Juricic E
title: The Orientation of Visual Space from the Perspective of Hummingbirds
why: Open access. Five Anna's hummingbirds (Calypte anna) and two rufous hummingbirds were measured for visual fields; harvest-24 logged the binocular width only as a group value (g) because the summariser did not separate the species. A full read can give Anna's own binocular width, the monocular and blind-area widths and the retinal map (retinal data came from Anna's only), which would close fov_h_deg and upgrade binocular_deg for Calypte.

authors: Lisney TJ, Iwaniuk AN, Kolominsky J, Wylie DR
title: Eye morphology and retinal topography in hummingbirds (Trochilidae: Aves)
why: Measured eye morphology in five hummingbird species and retinal topography in two (from the OpenAlex abstract start); the species list did not open, so it is not known that Calypte anna is among them. If it is, it can give interreceptor_deg or the data to compute it.

authors: Dingkun Liu, Huiqi Yan, Xuan Wang, Xiaohong Yan, Bing Zhou
title: Transcriptome Analysis Revealed Potential Regulatory Networks Underlying Corolla Movement in Mirabilis jalapa (Nyctaginaceae)
why: Open access paper on the opening and closing of the corolla of Mirabilis jalapa (four o'clock); the page did not open from this machine, and its abstract start (five corolla stages) names no light or time-of-day treatment, so it is not known that it measures a light or daily-rhythm response. If it does, it closes sense_light_nonvisual for Mirabilis. Authors are not confirmed. Authors from the Crossref record (desk Crossref run 3, 18 October 2026).
